articles.title: Where does a photoelectron’s energy come from?
articles.learningObjective: Use photon energy = work function + maximum kinetic energy to compare stopping potentials and thresholds.
articles.example: A photon supplies 5 eV to a surface needing 3 eV for escape.
articles.targetQuestionText: Light of wavelength λ gives a stopping potential of 3V₀. Light of wavelength 2λ gives V₀ for the same metal. What is the metal’s threshold wavelength?

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 1; Q42; question ID 69112142; PDF page 17
pyqs.independentSolution: E=φ+3eV0; E/2=φ+eV0. Subtraction gives E=4eV0, φ=eV0.

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 1; Q32; question ID 695278257; PDF page 11
pyqs.independentSolution: φ=hν0, so the lowest threshold frequency gives the smallest work function and largest Kmax for equal incident photon energy.

review.notes: The graph question is paraphrased into threshold frequencies, with illumination above all three thresholds stated explicitly. No emission is shown below the work function; negative kinetic energy is never displayed. articles.title: How much of a first-order reaction is finished?
articles.learningObjective: Distinguish fraction remaining from fraction reacted, and explain why two half-lives do not complete an ideal first-order reaction.
articles.example: 100 units of R become 50, 25 and 12.5 units after successive half-lives.
articles.targetQuestionText: For a first-order reaction R → P, what fraction of the original reactant has reacted after time t, if the rate constant is k?

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 1; Q57; question ID 695278282; PDF page 20
pyqs.independentSolution: Initial fraction 1; remaining exp(-kt); reacted 1-exp(-kt). At t=0 answer=0; at one half-life answer=1/2.

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 1; Q58; question ID 69112158; PDF page 23
pyqs.answer: Zero order: twice the initial half-life. First order: no finite exact completion time in the ideal model.
pyqs.independentSolution: Zero order R=R0-kt gives t_complete=R0/k=2 t_half. First order R=R0 exp(-kt) stays positive at finite t.

review.notes: The original Q58 option prints an awkward power-of-half-life notation for infinite completion. The article does not reproduce that dimensional expression: it clearly labels an adaptation and states the intended ideal-model limit in words. The keyed option ID and original image were checked. articles.title: How do you count functions that miss an output?
articles.learningObjective: Count missing-output cases and correct overlaps with inclusion-exclusion.
articles.example: Four labelled inputs assigned to a, b and c; the all-a function is counted in both missing-b and missing-c groups.
articles.targetQuestionText: Each input in the set 1, 2, 3, 4 is assigned to one output from a, b, c. How many such functions leave at least one output unused?

pyqs.locator: JEE Main Paper 1; 04 April 2026, Shift 1; Q4; question ID 695278229; PDF page 2
JEE Main Paper 1; 02 April 2026, Shift 1; Q6; question ID 6911216; PDF page 3
pyqs.independentSolution: 5^7 -5*4^7 +10*3^7 -10*2^7 +5 =16800; independently enumerated all 78125 candidate seven-digit sequences.

review.notes: Four labelled inputs remain the teaching example.
